rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 (kp 3.5) scored 125.8, below iteration 1 (kp 3.0) at 154.1. Progress fell on every track (oval 0.67 to 0.58, s-bend 0.30 to 0.25, slalom 0.08 to 0.08), and line_loss_events stayed at about 1.0 per run on all three tracks. Raising kp did not reduce line loss, so the 'raise kp to 4.0' rule in the Evaluator feedback is not supported. The oval finish in iteration 1 was a single lucky run (1 of 20), and the iteration 2 mean dropped on all tracks, so kp 3.5 looks slightly worse, not better.

Hypothesis: line loss is structural. With 12 mm footprints on a 20 mm pitch, the outer sensors often sit off the tape when the robot drifts, so the summed reading falls below 0.05 and the robot goes blind. Enlarging the footprint to 16 mm, which closes the 8 mm gaps between footprints, should keep at least one sensor on the tape through drift and reduce line-loss events.

Change: start from the best raced design (iteration 1) and change only sensor_size, from 0.012 to 0.016. kp returns to 3.0 because the iteration 2 result did not support 3.5. kd stays at 0.5, base_speed at 1.4, and the sensor positions, weights and line_loss mode are unchanged. Expected result: line_loss_events below about 0.5 per run, more progress on the s-bend and slalom, and a higher score than 154. Risk: a larger footprint averages the signal over more tape and may blunt steering sharpness at the bends. If oscillation stays around 0.3 or line loss persists, the next step is kd 0.3 to 0.4 or a 16 mm footprint with a narrower sensor spread.

Measurements wanted: per-track line_loss_events, completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error and steering_oscillation, so I can separate the footprint effect from the controller effect.
